title: http3: deprecate HTTP3_HEADER_NAME_CACHE
description:
Several changes that aim to reduce the memory usage and to increase robustness and readability:

1. Following up on the comment by John Thacker in f15c7ee1354d7ba51ea6e6579897e8fdcdfb7b87,
   simplified the caching of the HTTP/3 header fields:

   a. Deprecated the map `HTTP3_HEADER_NAME_CACHE`.
      The initial intent was to cache the header names and values separately,
      to further reduce the memory footprint. This intent never came to fruition.
      As a result, `HTTP3_HEADER_NAME_CACHE` was populated, but never used,
      causing the memory footprint to increase without any value.

   b. Moved away from the `http3_header_pstr` global variable.
      The global required special treatment, and was not strictly necessary.
      This MR moves the related functionality into a new function, `get_header_field_pstr`,
      which maintains a local scratch buffer with a `static` storage duration.
      The scratch buffer is only used for construction of the pstr strings.
      The rest of the dissector only uses cached pstrs owned by the `HTTP3_HEADER_CACHE` map.

2. General code cleanup:
  a. Removed some commented-out code.
  b. Cleaned up the includes.
  c. Cleaned up some of the code comments.
